name: Phuket
tagline: Andaman beaches, limestone bays and barefoot luxury.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: November to March is dry, calm and radiant; the May-October monsoon brings rain and rough seas, though October's Vegetarian Festival is a spectacle worth the weather.

ourTake.lede: Phuket splits sharply between the built-up west-coast beaches and the quieter north and east, and where you stay decides your entire trip, so choose carefully. Skip Patong unless nightlife is the point; the discreet resorts sit around Mai Khao, Cape Panwa and the headlands. Come November to April for the calm sea, and give Phuket Old Town a proper afternoon for its Sino-Portuguese streets and food.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a beach week with world-class resorts, island-hopping and quiet coves within reach.
ourTake.skipIf: You want an untouched, undiscovered shore; Phuket's coast is developed and busy in parts.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Amanpuri
credentials: MICHELIN Three Keys (2025), Phuket's only Three-Key hotel
items.description: The house that began Aman, Lanna pavilions above a private coconut headland, still the island's benchmark for calm.

items.name: Trisara
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Gold List 2024 & 2025 (only Thai resort listed)
items.description: Thirty-nine private-pool villas folded into a protected bay, extreme privacy, and the island's most decorated kitchens.

items.name: Rosewood Phuket
credentials: Travel + Leisure Luxury Awards Asia Pacific 2025, Top Beach & Island Resort in Thailand
items.description: A 600-metre private beach and 71 pavilions that dissolve into the hillside, Rosewood's Andaman idyll.

items.name: Six Senses Yao Noi
items.area: Koh Yao Noi, Phang Nga Bay
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Gold List (world's best places to stay)
items.description: Fifty-six clifftop pool villas facing the limestone karsts of Phang Nga Bay, the island beyond the island.

items.name: Iniala Beach House
items.description: Ten designer villas and residences on a wild beach north of the bridge, a private art-house of a hotel.

items.name: COMO Point Yamu
items.description: A Paola Navone-designed headland looking across Phang Nga Bay, cool, contemporary and gloriously away from the strip.

items.name: Anantara Layan Phuket Resort
items.description: A secluded palm-shaded bay of pool villas and hillside residences, Anantara at its most private.

items.name: InterContinental Phuket Resort
items.description: Seven Thai-inspired houses running from jungle to sand, with a private yacht and five pools.

items.name: Keemala
items.description: Thirty-eight clay cottages, tree-pool houses and tented villas woven into a rainforest hillside, pure fantasy, quietly done.

items.name: The Nai Harn Phuket
items.description: A crisp white headland hotel above one of the island's best beaches, polished and unfussy.

items.name: Andara Resort & Villas
items.description: Hillside suites and freestanding villas above Kamala Bay, space, privacy and a private chef if you want one.

items.name: The Slate
items.description: A tin-mining heritage turned into industrial-chic design, characterful, arty and close to the airport.

items.name: The Naka Island, a Luxury Collection Resort & Spa
items.description: A private-island retreat of pool villas a short boat ride from Phuket, barefoot seclusion within easy reach.

items.name: The Pavilions Phuket
items.description: Adults-only pool villas on a hillside above Layan, intimate, private and made for two.

items.name: The Racha
items.description: White-on-white minimalism on a clear-water island, the Andaman at its most postcard-blue.

items.name: Aleenta Phuket–Phang Nga Resort & Spa
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: Thirty beachfront villas and suites, every one facing the sea on a near-empty stretch of sand.

items.name: Banyan Tree Phuket
items.description: The resort that invented the private-pool villa in 1994, mature gardens, lagoons and a serious spa.

items.name: Angsana Laguna Phuket
items.description: A big, buzzy lagoon resort at the heart of Laguna, one of the island's longest free-form pools.

items.name: SALA Phuket Mai Khao Beach Resort
items.description: Sino-Portuguese pool villas on the island's longest, quietest beach, an easy, private escape.

items.name: Renaissance Phuket Resort & Spa
items.description: A relaxed low-rise beach resort on Mai Khao, pool villas and gardens without the crowds.

items.name: The Big Buddha (Ming Mongkol Buddha) on Nakkerd Hill
items.description: A 45-metre white-marble Buddha crowning the hill between Chalong, Kata and Rawai, with a 360-degree panorama that lets the whole family take in half the island at once. Dress modestly (shawls provided), come at golden hour, and have your driver hold at the quieter lower terrace while grandparents rest.

items.name: Wat Chalong (Wat Chaithararam)
items.description: Phuket's grandest and most revered temple, a serene complex of gilded pavilions culminating in a 60-metre pagoda that houses a fragment of the Buddha's bone. Fifteen minutes from the Big Buddha, it pairs naturally into a calm, multi-generational morning of merit-making before the heat.

items.name: Promthep Cape at sunset
items.description: The island's southernmost headland, where crowds gather each evening as the sun drops into the Andaman behind rocky islets. Skip the car park scrum: charter a sunset catamaran or have your villa's chef pack a chilled hamper for the grassy point just above the lighthouse.

items.name: Old Phuket Town's Sino-Portuguese quarter
items.description: A photogenic grid of restored tin-baron shophouses in sherbet colours, best explored on a slow, cool-of-the-morning walk with a private heritage guide. The pace and history suit older travellers; the cafes and boutiques keep younger ones happy.

items.name: Thalang Road
items.description: The old town's 350-metre historic artery, lined with the best-preserved Sino-Portuguese facades on the island and the first street here to bury its power lines underground. It threads together tea houses, textile shops and gold-leaf shrines in one strollable ribbon.

items.name: Soi Romanee
items.description: A once-notorious lane now reborn as the town's prettiest, its pastel two-storey shophouses spilling with bougainvillea, artisan coffee and ice-cream parlours. It is the single most-photographed street in Phuket and a gentle five-minute stroll off Thalang Road.

items.name: Sunday Walking Street (Lard Yai)
items.description: Every Sunday from 4pm, Thalang Road closes to traffic and fills with hawker carts, live music and Hokkien-Thai street food beneath the lantern-lit shophouses. Ask your guide to steer the family to the vegetarian and fresh-fruit stalls, plentiful here thanks to Phuket's own veg-food tradition.

items.name: Patong Beach
items.description: Phuket's most famous and most energetic beach, a broad two-kilometre curve backed by every convenience. Base here only if you want buzz; otherwise it makes a lively half-day of jet-skis and beach clubs before retreating to a quieter west-coast villa.

items.name: Kata Beach and Kata Noi
items.description: Two gently curving, palm-fringed bays that are calmer and more polished than Patong, with reliable swimming and easy surf lessons for teens in the green season. The stretch is a favourite of families who want beach days without the noise.

items.name: Karon Beach
items.description: A wide, quieter three-kilometre run of squeaky white sand that stays uncrowded even in season, backed by low-key resorts and lagoon parkland. Long enough for a proper morning walk before the sun turns fierce.

items.name: Surin Beach
items.description: Once nicknamed 'Millionaire's Row', a compact golden bay flanked by Phuket's smartest beach resorts and clubs. The most discreet-luxury stretch on the coast, ideal if you want a chic sundowner without the mainstream crowds.

items.name: Kamala Beach
items.description: A relaxed, family-friendly bay just south of Surin with a genuine village feel and calm swimming water. It anchors the low-key luxury enclave of Phuket's northwest, within easy reach of the island's headline beach clubs.

items.name: Nai Harn Beach
items.description: A postcard cove in the island's south, backed by a lagoon and monastery and consistently rated among Phuket's most beautiful. Sheltered and swimmable, it draws a quieter, in-the-know crowd and sits minutes from Promthep Cape.

items.name: Freedom Beach
items.description: A secluded 300-metre ribbon of powder sand reachable only by boat or a steep jungle path, which keeps it blissfully empty. Charter a longtail or speedboat from Patong for a private half-day; it is the island's most accessible 'hidden' beach.

items.name: Karon Viewpoint (Three Beaches Hill)
items.description: The island's classic postcard lookout, framing the three arcs of Kata Noi, Kata and Karon in one turquoise sweep. An easy roadside stop between beaches and the south, best in clear morning light.

items.name: Windmill Viewpoint
items.description: A cliff-edge lookout just south of Karon Viewpoint, above Ya Nui and Nai Harn, with sweeping views over Rawai and the offshore islands. Quieter than its famous neighbour and a fine spot to pause on the coastal drive south.

items.name: Phang Nga Bay by private boat
items.description: A dreamscape of sheer limestone karsts rising from emerald water an hour north of Phuket, best seen away from the day-boat crowds. A private yacht or speedboat charter lets the family set its own pace through the caves and hidden lagoons, with a chef and shade on board.

items.name: James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan / Koh Tapu)
items.description: The needle-thin islet made famous by 'The Man with the Golden Gun', still one of the bay's signature sights. Time a private charter for early morning or late afternoon to have the viewpoint largely to yourselves before the tour armada arrives.

items.name: Sea-cave canoeing in Phang Nga Bay
items.description: The quiet highlight of any bay trip: a skilled paddler steers you through low sea caves into secret 'hong' lagoons ringed by jungle cliffs, in near silence. Gentle enough for grandparents and children alike, and unforgettable at dusk when the bats emerge.

items.name: Koh Panyee floating village
items.description: A Muslim fishing community of about 1,600 built entirely on stilts at the foot of a towering cliff, complete with a mosque, seafood restaurants and a famous floating football pitch. A vivid, humane counterpoint to the bay's natural drama.

items.name: Phi Phi Islands day trip
items.description: The Andaman's most celebrated islands, ringed by jade water, karst walls and coral gardens roughly 45 minutes by speedboat from Phuket. Charter privately and start at dawn to reach the snorkelling coves and viewpoints before the fleets, then lunch quietly offshore.

items.name: Maya Bay
items.description: The luminous cliff-ringed cove made globally famous by 'The Beach', now carefully rationed to protect its recovering reef. Landings are via the Loh Samah back beach with timed slots and no swimming inside the bay; note it closes each 1 August to 30 September for regeneration.

items.name: Similan Islands (seasonal)
items.description: A national-park archipelago of glass-clear water, granite boulders and world-class reefs, open only 15 October to 15 May each year. A long but spectacular day out from Phuket, best on a fast private catamaran; among Southeast Asia's finest snorkelling and diving.

items.name: Racha Yai (Raya) Island
items.description: A calm, clear-water island south of Phuket prized for easy snorkelling and swimming off soft white sand, reachable in under an hour. Its sheltered bays and single luxury resort make it a serene private-charter day escape.

items.name: Coral Island (Koh Hae)
items.description: A close, family-friendly island just fifteen minutes off Chalong pier, with two gentle beaches and shallow reef ideal for first-time snorkellers and children. Perfect for a half-day charter when you want sea and coral without a long crossing.

items.name: Naka Island (Naka Yai)
items.description: A tranquil island a short hop off Phuket's northeast, home to a serene luxury resort and a quiet Saturday-Sunday morning market. It suits couples and families wanting seclusion and spa time rather than crowds.

items.name: Phuket Elephant Sanctuary
items.description: Phuket's first true ethical sanctuary, where rescued elephants roam free with no riding and, from April 2026, no feeding interactions at all: you observe from a canopy walkway and learn at the on-site hospital. Endorsed by National Geographic and World Animal Protection, it is the responsible choice for multi-generational visits.

items.name: Wat Phra Thong (the half-buried Buddha)
items.description: A quietly atmospheric temple built around a gilded Buddha that, by legend, cannot be fully dug out of the earth, so only its head and shoulders show. An offbeat, uncrowded stop north of the airport for those drawn to Phuket's older spiritual life.

items.name: Jui Tui Shrine and Bang Neow Shrine
items.description: The two great Chinese Taoist shrines at the heart of the old town and the ceremonial core of Phuket's famous Vegetarian Festival each autumn. Richly decorated and incense-filled, they add depth to any old-town walk.

items.name: Thai Hua Museum
items.description: A beautifully restored former Chinese-language school that tells the story of Phuket's tin-mining Peranakan heritage in an elegant Sino-Portuguese mansion. A cool, air-conditioned hour that gives the old town's streets their context.

items.name: Phuket Vegetarian Festival
items.description: A dramatic nine-day Taoist festival each September or October when devotees observe a strict plant-based diet and perform intense street processions. The rigorous vegetarian offerings citywide make this a rare and comfortable time for Jain and vegetarian travellers.

items.name: Muay Thai training or a ringside night
items.description: Thailand's national fighting art, available either as a private morning session at a serious camp or as an electric evening at a stadium like Bangla or Patong Boxing Stadium. A private coach can tailor a fun, safe session for energetic teenagers.

items.name: A traditional Thai spa afternoon
items.description: Phuket's marquee resorts and standalone maisons offer some of Asia's finest spa rituals, from herbal-compress massage to hammam-style scrubs. Arrange a private couples' or family suite for an unhurried afternoon of quiet luxury.

items.name: Simon Cabaret
items.description: Phuket's long-running, lavishly costumed transgender cabaret, a polished hour of feathers, sequins and lip-synced spectacle that has become a Southeast Asian institution. Family-friendly and easy to book into a private box; three nightly show times.

items.name: Bangla Road
items.description: Patong's neon-lit pedestrian strip, the loud, unfiltered epicentre of Phuket nightlife, worth a brief look-in for its sheer spectacle rather than a long stay. Most discerning travellers prefer a single curious walk-through before retiring to a quiet rooftop bar.

items.name: Sunday sundowners at a west-coast beach club
items.description: The Kamala-Surin coast holds Phuket's most stylish beach clubs, where infinity pools meet the Andaman and DJs play as the sun drops. Reserve a daybed or cabana for a relaxed, grown-up afternoon that still works for older children.

items.name: Chillva Market
items.description: A hip, local-favourite night market of repurposed shipping-container stalls, street food and live music, busiest Wednesday to Saturday evenings. A younger, more contemporary scene than the heritage Sunday market, and refreshingly free of tourist mark-ups.

items.name: Private yacht charter around the southern islands
items.description: The definitive way to see Phuket's waters: a crewed motor yacht or catamaran for the day, threading between Coral, Racha and the Phi Phi group with a chef, water toys and shade on board. The itinerary bends to your family, dietary needs included.

items.name: Ao Sane and Ya Nui beaches
items.description: Two tiny, boulder-framed coves near Promthep Cape with the best shore snorkelling on the island and a fraction of the crowds. Bring your own masks for a quiet morning in clear, fish-filled water before the day-trippers arrive.

items.name: Laem Singh Beach
items.description: A jewel-like cove tucked below the coastal road, now reached via a private beach-club path or by boat, with calm water and a genuine hidden-gem feel. Best arranged through a resort concierge for the smoothest access.

items.name: Rang Hill (Khao Rang) viewpoint
items.description: A leafy, breezy hill just above the old town with a sweeping view over the rooftops to Chalong Bay and a couple of relaxed cafes. An easy, uncrowded sunset alternative close to town when you don't want to drive to the coast.

items.name: Ban Bang Rong and the northeast mangroves
items.description: A peaceful Muslim fishing community on the quiet east coast where you can kayak or take a longtail through mangrove channels and eat fresh seafood over the water. A gentle, authentic half-day far from the beach resorts.

items.name: Khao Phra Thaeo rainforest and Bang Pae Waterfall
items.description: Phuket's last virgin rainforest, home to a modest waterfall and a gibbon rehabilitation project you can visit responsibly. A green, cooler counterpoint to the beaches for families who want a short jungle walk.

items.name: Cape Panwa and the far southeast
items.description: A quiet, wooded headland of luxury villas and calm coves with an aquarium at its tip, well away from the west-coast bustle. A serene base or half-day drive when you want the island's gentler, more residential side.

items.name: PRU
items.description: Chef Jimmy Ophorst's 'Plant. Raise. Understand.', the island's first star, built entirely on its own farm and coast.

items.name: Aulis Phuket by Simon Rogan
items.description: Simon Rogan's fifteen-seat chef's table, his farm-to-table philosophy transplanted to the Andaman coast.

items.name: Jampa
items.description: A zero-waste, live-fire kitchen in the middle of its own organic farm, sustainability as the whole point.

items.name: Jaras
items.description: Chef 'Nui' Srivorakul's photogenic modern southern Thai, the first Thai kitchen to partner with WWF Thailand.

items.name: hom
items.description: A fermentation-led modern Thai room exploring the depth of the island's larder.

items.name: Suay Cherngtalay
items.description: Chef Noi Tammasak's creative modern Thai, one of Phuket's most-loved kitchens for years.

items.name: Samut
items.description: Modern Thai and Andaman seafood in the quiet south, precise, coastal, of-the-island.

items.name: Royd
items.description: A modern southern-Thai kitchen giving Phuket's own recipes a fine-dining voice in the old town.

items.name: Blue Elephant Phuket
items.description: Royal Thai cuisine in a grand Sino-Portuguese mansion, the old town's most theatrical dining room.

items.name: L'Arome by the Sea
items.description: Contemporary French with an Andaman view, polished, romantic and quietly ambitious.

items.name: Bisou Phuket
items.description: A modern French room on the Bang Tao strip, refined cooking amid the beach-club energy.

items.name: Acqua
items.description: A long-standing modern-Italian fixture with a serious cellar above Patong.

items.name: Five Olives
items.description: Contemporary Italian cooking done with care on the Bang Tao coast.

items.name: La Gaetana
items.description: A tiny, personal Italian trattoria that has long outpunched its size in the old town.

items.name: Tambu
items.description: Modern Indian cooking with real ambition, a rare fine-dining Indian voice on the island.

items.name: The Smokaccia Laboratory
items.description: A modern, smoke-and-fire-driven kitchen doing some of Surin's most inventive cooking.

items.name: Wagyu Steakhouse
items.description: A precise, cuts-led steakhouse for the member who wants marbled beef done properly.

items.name: Ta Khai
items.description: A recreated fishing-village kitchen inside Rosewood, southern Thai recipes cooked the old way.

items.name: Talung Thai
items.description: Long-running southern-Thai home cooking with a devoted following.

items.name: Bucha Gallery & Restaurant
items.description: Southern-Thai cooking in a gallery-like room away from the beaches.

items.name: HEH Restaurant
items.description: A modern Thai-and-seafood room bringing a young energy to the old town.

items.name: One Chun
items.description: The old town's most beloved kitchen for Phuket-Hokkien home cooking, moo hong, crab curry, and heritage.

items.name: The Charm
items.description: Refined Phuket and southern-Thai cooking in a handsome old-town setting.

items.name: Chom Chan
items.description: Phuket and southern-Thai flavours cooked with real depth, a Bib favourite in town.

items.name: Raya
items.description: A grand old Sino-Portuguese mansion serving classic Phuket dishes, crab curry and heritage in equal measure.

items.name: Naam Yoi
items.description: Generations-old local and southern-Thai cooking, prized for its balanced, honest flavours.

items.name: Mor Mu Dong
items.description: A stilted seafood shack over the mangroves, southern-Thai fishing-village cooking at its most authentic.

items.name: Salaloy Seafood
items.description: A long-loved beachside seafood house on the southern shore, fresh, simple, unpretentious.

items.name: Go Benz
items.description: The island's cult stop for noodle soup and rice porridge, a decades-old institution.

items.name: Khao Tom Thanon Dibuk
items.description: Late-night rice soup and southern-Thai comfort food on Dibuk Road, a local ritual.

items.name: Niyom Salt Grilled Duck
items.description: Thirty-odd charcoal-roasted ducks a day, tender and salt-crisp, a single-dish master.

items.name: Krua Baan Platong
items.description: Intensely flavoured Phuket home cooking from local ingredients, the essence of the island on a plate.

items.name: Kin Kub Ei
items.description: Southern-Thai family recipes passed down the generations, balanced and quietly excellent.

items.name: Pathongko Mae Pranee
items.description: A morning institution for pathongko and hot soy milk, breakfast the Phuket way.

items.name: A Pong Mae Sunee
items.description: Crisp-edged coconut a-pong griddle cakes from a stall the Michelin inspectors sought out.

items.name: Roti Thaew Nam
items.description: Flaky roti and Thai-Muslim curries on an old-town lane, a cult breakfast and lunch stop.

items.name: Go La Hokkien Fried Noodles
items.description: A single-wok master turning out the island's definitive Hokkien fried noodles.

items.name: Prawn Noodle Ao Ke
items.description: A specialist doing one thing, rich Hokkien prawn noodles, better than anyone on the island.

items.name: Catch Beach Club
credentials: Phuket's original beach club (opened Surin, 2012), the venue credited with launching the island's beach-club scene, by Twinpalms
items.description: Twinpalms' beachfront original, the club that started Phuket's whole beach-club culture, still the name against which the rest are measured.

items.name: Rock Salt
credentials: The signature beachfront bar-restaurant of The Nai Harn (MICHELIN One Key hotel), on Nai Harn Beach
items.description: The Nai Harn's beachfront terrace above one of the island's finest bays, an unhurried sundowner in the quiet south.

items.name: The Fool Speakeasy
credentials: Best Bar in Phuket/Samui, Bangkok Bar Show Awards 2025
items.description: A tarot-themed hideaway in an old shophouse, twenty-two Major Arcana cocktails and the most serious mixing on the island.

items.name: Baba Nest
credentials: Named among the world's best beach/rooftop bars by CNN; voted a global top-three beach bar (CNNgo)
items.description: A rooftop deck 60 metres above the sea, ringed by its own infinity moat, a 360-degree sunset the world has decided is among the best anywhere.

items.name: Vanilla Sky
credentials: Long-standing rooftop bar atop Cape Sienna Gourmet Hotel, a recognised fixture on Phuket's rooftop-bar circuit, 180-degree Kamala Bay view
items.description: Cape Sienna's clifftop rooftop with a full sweep of Kamala Bay, cocktails as the light goes over the Andaman.

items.name: XANA Beach Club
credentials: The beach club of Angsana Laguna Phuket, one of Bang Tao's established day-to-night party venues
items.description: Angsana Laguna's beachfront pool club, day-to-night DJs and a young, lively crowd on the Bang Tao sand.

plan.heading: 3 days in Phuket, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Check in at Amanpuri on Pansea headland or Trisara, then a slow morning by your private pool as the day settles.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A guided walk through Old Phuket Town's Sino-Portuguese shophouses on Thalang Road, ending with kopi at a Peranakan café.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sunset and dinner at PRU, the island's Michelin-starred farm-to-table room at Trisara.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A private yacht from the resort marina out to Phang Nga Bay, threading the limestone karsts and sea caves by kayak.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Anchor for a quiet swim and a fresh seafood lunch aboard, away from the day-tripper flotillas.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Back on land, dinner at Suay by Chef Noi or a beach barbecue laid out privately on the sand.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A long spa morning and a swim, the island at its slowest.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A final lunch of southern Thai curries, then unhurried packing.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: An early sundowner at Baba Nest before the transfer to the airport.

items.name: Mai Khao / Natai
items.description: The quiet northern beaches with the discreet luxury resorts and long empty sand; for privacy over nightlife.

items.name: Cape Panwa / Ao Yon
items.description: A calm southeastern headland of secluded resorts and marinas; suits couples and yacht days.

items.name: Phuket Old Town
items.description: The colourful Sino-Portuguese quarter with the best local food and cafés; a cultural counterpoint to the beaches.

events.name: Phuket Vegetarian Festival
events.note: The nine-day Nine Emperor Gods festival, with white-clad devotees, temple processions and dramatic firewalking rituals.

events.name: Loy Krathong
events.note: The festival of lights, marked along the island's beaches with floating candlelit krathong at dusk.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: The quiet luxury sits on the west coast, Amanpuri and the Cape Panwa headland over busy Patong; November to April is dry and calm, while the May–October monsoon brings strong currents and closed beaches on some days.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: You arrive at Phuket International (HKT); a private car reaches most west-coast resorts in thirty to sixty minutes, and a resort-arranged speedboat or seaplane is the elegant line to the islands.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: Take a private car with driver, the island is large and taxis are inconsistent, and switch to a chartered longtail or yacht for Phang Nga Bay and the surrounding islands.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: An AIS or TrueMove eSIM gives solid 4G/5G along the coasts; villa and resort wifi is dependable.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Thai baht (THB); resorts and restaurants take cards, but carry cash for boatmen, markets and beach vendors; tipping is modest and discretionary.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: December to March is the dry, calm-sea season for the beaches and island-hopping; avoid the Andaman monsoon from May to October, worst in September when seas are rough and ferries are routinely cancelled.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No non-stop from India; the clean routing is via Bangkok on Thai Airways or Air India (about 4.5h to BKK, then roughly 1h 20m south). Bangkok Airways serves Phuket well on the domestic leg with its own lounges. Overall door-to-door is a half-day with one connection.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No mandatory vaccinations; routine jabs plus Hepatitis A and Typhoid advised. Safe and relaxed. Bottled water only; sea conditions in monsoon months can be genuinely dangerous, so heed red flags.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian is easy at resorts and better restaurants; Jain is possible with advance notice. Indian food is available in the tourist belts (Patong, Bang Tao) though less refined than Bangkok. Best handled through your resort or a private chef for consistency.
